title: MAST: A Multi-View Alignment Strategy for Optimal Transport-Based Contrastive Clustering of Short Text
subcategory: contrastive short-text clustering with graph views and optimal-transport pseudo-labels
problem: Contrastive clustering relies on augmentations of limited semantic granularity and lacks global optimisation of cluster assignments, so pseudo-label noise accumulates on short, sparse texts.
architecture: SBERT encoder; sentence-level and cluster-level graphs (two-layer GCN) give structure-enhanced views aligned with original and augmented embeddings by a multi-view contrastive loss with structure-aware negative reweighting and intermediate-layer negatives; Student-t soft assignments with high-confidence guidance; optimal-transport pseudo-label alignment; final k-means on learned embeddings.

datasets.name: GoogleNews-TS / GoogleNews-T / GoogleNews-S
datasets.details: news titles/snippets; G-T and G-S highly imbalanced

key_results: Best ACC/NMI on all six datasets, e.g. AgNews ACC 88.34 / NMI 68.39 vs 87.85 / 66.70 for FNSCC; Tweet ACC 90.41 / NMI 93.87 vs 83.62 / 90.38 for FNSCC.
On GoogleNews-T ACC 80.14 vs 72.72 (FNSCC); improvements significant under a paired t-test (p < 0.005).
strengths: Couples representation learning and assignment refinement in one objective.
Larger gains on the most imbalanced and sparsest datasets.

limitations.text: Multi-view structural modelling adds computational overhead over instance-level contrastive methods.
Relies on fixed hyperparameters to balance contrastive and clustering objectives.
Structural views built from cosine similarity and soft assignments capture only coarse relations.
Number of clusters K is given to the model (k-means and K learnable centres).
